anime_title: Even the Student Council Has Its Holes!
episode_title: Pure Chaos in the Council Room and That Unhinged Timing
pullquote: Passione isn't just firing off ecchi comedy tropes; they're tuning every gag with razor-sharp comedic timing that hits like a freight train.
quick_take: Passione isn't just firing off ecchi comedy tropes; they're tuning every gag with razor-sharp comedic timing that hits like a freight train.
one_sentence_verdict: A relentless clinic in gag timing and expressive animation that proves why this misfit council is one of the sharpest late-night comedies running.
synopsis_paragraphs: You know that split-second before a punchline lands where everything freezes and your brain realizes disaster is guaranteed? Episode 8 lives in that exact space. The rhythm here doesn't mess around. We are deep into the back half of the season now, and instead of coasting on autopilot, the show cranks the throttle on Fujinasu Academy's weirdest council. The tension between Ume Mizunoe just praying to pass his science requirements and the sheer unhinged energy of the room reaches absolute boiling point.

It’s not just noise, either. What makes this episode hit so hard is the sheer confidence in its escalation. One second Ume is clutching his sanity while trying to handle standard council admin tasks, and the next, the entire room derails into manic slapstick. The transition doesn't give you room to breathe. You get hit with high-speed banter, a sudden deadpan stare, and then an explosion of physical comedy that feels completely earned because the show spent weeks setting up these exact character flaws.
sakuga_paragraphs: - **Craft point: Dead silence right before the punch.** Director Naoyuki Tatsuwa and sound director Satoshi Motoyama pull off an absolute masterclass in comic pacing here. Instead of plastering Tomoki Kikuya's upbeat score over every second of action, they cut the audio completely dry on key reaction shots. That sudden drop of ambient room noise turns an ordinary visual gag into an absolute gut-punch because your brain expects music and gets slapped with pure, awkward silence.

- **Craft point: Kinetic snapping on character expressions.** Take a close look at how Ryou Imamura's character designs are animated when things go wild. The team skips easing frames on fast turns, snapping characters instantly from soft, rounded slice-of-life expressions into stretched, exaggerated smear poses. Cinematographer Junpei Takatsu matches those snappy cuts with quick focal shifts that mimic the sudden panel switches of a manga page, keeping the kinetic energy buzzing without ever turning into visual clutter.
story_paragraphs: - **「テンポ良すぎて草」 (The tempo is way too good, lol):** Midnight live threads on 5ch and X latched right onto the frantic pacing. In Japanese net slang, "kusa" (草, meaning grass) represents endless laughter, and fans were spamming it across reaction boards the second the mid-episode argument spun completely out of control without dropping a single beat.

- **「作画の圧がすごい」 (The visual pressure is insane):** A frequent shout on late-night roundup feeds whenever Passione goes all-in on animated physical comedy. Fans kept highlighting how the episode refuses to rest on still frames or simple mouth flaps, pouring heavy key animation into tiny secondary gestures, wild hand movements, and hilarious background reactions.
voice_paragraphs: - Haruka Shiraishi's deadpan snap as Hisako Kotobuki playing off Shougo Sakata's frantic, fraying delivery as Ume Mizunoe steals the spotlight. Sakata doesn't just play Ume as a generic screamer; he injects this exhausted, wheezing breath into his straight-man rebuttals that sells just how much soul-crushing damage the council's antics are doing to his sanity. It gives Miyu Tomita's stray-cat squeaks as Komaro Michinoku and Hiyori Kouno's smug teasing as Tan Otori the perfect sounding board to bounce off of.
takeaway_paragraphs: A relentless clinic in gag timing and expressive animation that proves why this misfit council is one of the sharpest late-night comedies running. You can catch the chaos streaming officially right now on Bilibili TV.
